method: SmolLM2-135M, ctx=2048, Q8_0, split=8, 32-token generation. At step i, cycle through layers [0..7] round-robin; issue an ASYNC copy (ggml_backend_tensor_set_async) of that layer's real K/V bytes to a fresh GPU scratch tensor, immediately call llama_decode for the current token (so its compute is enqueued right after the async submission), then ggml_backend_synchronize(). Deterministic, predeclared schedule -- no adaptive policy. 5 repetitions.
overlap_achieved_detail: Residual sync_wait_ms (time NOT hidden behind decode compute) is 0.0525 ms mean over 32 copy+decode steps -- effectively zero compared to the copy issue cost or a synchronous equivalent. Nearly all of the copy latency was hidden behind the decode call's own GPU work.
caveat: As with sync_stall.json, this measures wall-clock overlap of the COPY MACHINERY with real decode compute -- it does NOT mean the prefetched bytes are consumed by decode (classification B holds identically here; this prototype never claims live rebind). It answers 'can copy latency be hidden' in isolation from 'does the copy affect output', which are two different questions.
